title: VPC private deployment: Post-deploy Sanity & Model-Load Test Suite
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description: Goal: Implement an automated post-deploy test suite and verification workflow for Private (VPC) deployments created by our Terraform modules. The suite should run as a post-apply step (CI job or operator hook) and validate API readiness, model artifact loadability, and a small set of smoke patterns representative of customer traffic. The outcome should be a clear PASS/FAIL with diagnostic artifacts (logs, stack traces, Grafana snapshots) and guidance for automated rollback or human intervention. Scope: - API readiness probe (HTTP health + readiness endpoints, TLS cert check) - Model-load validation against a representative model bundle (load into runtime, warm KV cache, verify generation) - Lightweight load test (10–50 concurrent requests for 30s, assert latency P95 < configured SLO) - Smoke test set (5 canned prompts for correctness and no runtime errors) - Integration with Terraform outputs and the deployment CI pipeline Deliverables: - A reusable test runner script (python/bash) and a container image published to our internal registry - Terraform module hooks (outputs or null_resource with local-exec) examples for invoking tests after apply - CI job templates (CircleCI/GitHub Actions) for Private deploy pipelines - Runbook: how to interpret failures and trigger rollback/manual remediation - Grafana dashboard links and required metrics to collect (in README) Constraints & trade-offs considered: - Avoid heavy load tests that slow down automations; keep baseline smoke quick but conservative - Do not require full model downloads for extremely large models; support a 'sanity bundle' (small quantized checkpoint) to validate runtime path - Tests must be idempotent and safe to re-run on the same cluster
acceptance_criteria: Post-deploy job returns PASS within 10 minutes on a healthy cluster
API readiness: /health and /ready return 200 and consistent TLS certificate CN matches expected domain
Model load: runtime reports model state=READY and kv_cache warmup completes without OOM for the sanity bundle
Load test: 30s run at 20 concurrent sessions with P95 latency < configured SLO (default 250ms) OR documented SLO override
Smoke generation: 5 prompts produce syntactically valid JSON/text and no runtime exceptions
Artifacts: logs + trace id + link to grafana snapshot uploaded to CI run on FAILURE
runbook_commands:
# Example: curl health endpoints
curl -sSf -o /dev/null https://private-api.company.internal/health || exit 1
curl -sSf -o /dev/null https://private-api.company.internal/ready || exit 1

# Terraform: expose outputs then call test container
terraform output -json private_deploy_info > tf_outputs.json
./scripts/postdeploy/run_sanity.sh tf_outputs.json

# Run model load check via containerized runner
docker run --rm -e TF_OUTPUTS=tf_outputs.json ghcr.io/redwood-inference/postdeploy-sanity:2026-03 ./runner.py --check-model --model-id small-sanity-bundle

# Lightweight load test using vegeta (example)
echo '{"method":"POST","url":"https://private-api.company.internal/generate","body":"{\"prompt\":\"hello\"}"}' | vegeta attack -duration=30s -rate=20 | vegeta report --type=json > vegeta_report.json

# Upload failure artifacts to CI build (pseudo)
ci_upload_tool --files logs/*.log vegeta_report.json grafana_snapshot.png --build-id $CI_BUILD_ID
